title: P0 Hosted API — Heartbeat queue buildup incident review (2026-03-20)
summary: Between 08:04 and 09:12 UTC on 2026-03-20 the hosted API experienced a sustained latency spiral and elevated 5xx errors for streaming sessions. Root cause was a rapid buildup of messages in the internal heartbeat processing queue (heartbeat-consumer-shard), caused by a combination of a client-side SDK rolling update that removed jitter and a concurrent config rollout that disabled soft backpressure on that route. The queue backlog caused head-of-line blocking in the streaming path, producing high tail latency and downstream timeouts.
impact: Approximately 18% of active streaming sessions saw degraded token delivery p95 latency increase from ~120ms to >2s and intermittent 502/504 errors. Generated customer-facing errors increased across the EU and US regions. Internal error budget burned substantially; several paying customers reported product-impacting regressions.
timeline:
08:02 UTC — Monitoring alert: streaming p95 latency > 1s in eu-west-1.
08:04 UTC — On-call alerted (pager).
08:06 UTC — Channel created and initial triage by on-call SRE (Maya). Identified large rise in queue length for heartbeat-consumer-shard-*.
08:10 UTC — Noted recent config rollout 07:58 UTC disabling soft backpressure on /v1/stream/heartbeat-route (deploy config: cfg-2026-03-20-14).
08:12 UTC — Observed SDK version v2.7.1 rollout to customers starting ~07:50 UTC; SDK removed randomized jitter on client heartbeats (internal bug #SDK-945).
08:20 UTC — Applied emergency mitigation: rolled back config disabling soft backpressure to previous config (cfg-2026-03-19-79).
08:28 UTC — Increased heartbeat-consumer shard count from 8 → 12 to help drain backlog.
08:35 UTC — Introduced temporary rate limit (per-client) on heartbeat route to reduce burstiness while backlog drained.
08:47 UTC — p95 latency trending down but still above baseline. Continued backlog drain.
09:12 UTC — Metrics returned to acceptable thresholds; paging closed and incident declared mitigated.
11:00 UTC — Post-incident follow-up meeting scheduled and action items captured.
detection: Primary detection via streaming p95 latency alert (alert id: AL-STREAM-P95-EU). Secondary signals: queue_length_heartbeat_consumer, consumer_lag, increase in 502/504 for streaming endpoints. Pager fired automatically from latency alert (~08:04 UTC).
root_cause_summary: The immediate root cause was head-of-line blocking due to heartbeat-consumer queues filling faster than consumers could process. This was a multi-factor failure: (1) client SDK rollout removed jitter causing synchronized heartbeat bursts, (2) a recent config change temporarily disabled soft backpressure which would have smoothed bursts, and (3) autoscaling did not react quickly enough because shard scaling thresholds are conservative, so backlog growth outran scaling. The combination created a transient overload on the streaming path leading to high latency and 5xx errors.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Rolled back the config change that removed soft backpressure on the heartbeat route (cfg rollback at 08:20 UTC). 2) Manually increased consumer shard count (08:28 UTC) to parallelize processing and reduce per-shard queue depth. 3) Applied a temporary per-client rate limit and short circuit for malformed heartbeat messages to reduce noise while system recovered. 4) Requested client SDK teams to halt v2.7.1 rollout to customers and push a hotfix reintroducing jitter.
remediation_steps: Patch client SDK v2.7.1 to reintroduce randomized jitter for heartbeat intervals (owner: client-sdk-team, ticket SDK-945)
Adjust auto-scaler policy for heartbeat-consumer to scale more aggressively on queue length (owner: infra-autoscale, ticket SRE-1428)
Add a deployment guard that prevents disabling soft backpressure for streaming routes without an automated canary (owner: eng-platform, ticket PLAT-811)
Create a pre-deploy checklist item requiring SRE sign-off for config changes affecting streaming backpressure (owner: eng-sre, ticket SRE-1430)
Add per-route burst protection in the edge/proxy layer with tunable buckets for heartbeat traffic (owner: edge-team, ticket EDGE-264)
Add histogram and alert for per-shard head-of-line latency and consumer lag to detect early queueing (owner: observability, ticket OBS-990)
long_term_actions: Implement graceful degradation for streaming sessions when heartbeat processing is delayed (e.g., return partial frames rather than blocking) — design doc due 2026-04-10 (owner: serving-runtime)
Run a chaos experiment simulating synchronized heartbeat bursts to validate autoscaler and backpressure fixes (owner: eng-sre, due 2026-05-01)
Automate SDK rollout detection by monitoring client-side heartbeat variance signals (owner: client-platform, due 2026-04-20)
Improve runbook to include explicit checks and playbooks for heartbeat/keepalive routes (owner: eng-sre, due 2026-03-28)
runbook_changes: Add step: validate heartbeat route backpressure setting before merging config changes. Include checklist item with link to canary dashboard.
Add playbook: if queue_length > threshold and p95 latency rising, immediately enable temporary per-client rate limiting and increase shard count. Provide exact commands and thresholds.
Add guidance: check recent client SDK rollout notes (internal SDK registry) when debugging heartbeat/keepalive anomalies.
Document rollback steps for cfg-*. Example commands and expected signals to confirm rollback success.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Create new alert: per-shard consumer_lag > 5s for 1 minute (severity P1)
Add synthetic canary that simulates randomized heartbeats at production scale to detect jitter regressions (owner: observability)
Expose heartbeat variance metric to release dashboards so SDK releases can be correlated with server-side load spikes
postmortem_conclusions: This incident shows the risk of low-latency, high-throughput control traffic (heartbeats) when coordination between client SDK behavior and server-side backpressure is weak. The individual failures were recoverable, but their interaction created a P0 due to lack of deployment guards and conservative autoscaler thresholds. With the immediate mitigations and the planned follow-ups, similar incidents should be detected earlier and contained automatically.
pager_notes: On-call notes: 1) First signal was streaming p95; check queue_length_heartbeat_consumer early. 2) If queue growing rapidly, look for overlapping deploys (cfg-* or sdk rollouts) in the preceding 30 minutes. 3) Apply rollback of backpressure-affecting configs before scaling if safe to do so. 4) Communicate customer-facing status transparently; customers were notified via status.redwood.ai incident page.
post_incident_meeting: 2026-03-21 11:00 UTC — Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Zhao, Priya Menon, Lucas Romero, Anya Kuznetsov, client-sdk lead. Agenda: review timeline, assign owners, review SDK hotfix progress.

notes_to_self: Keep example query snippets for increasing shard count handy in the runbook. Consider a small CLI helper to do safe rollbacks of config flags that impact backpressure. Validate that per-client rate limits are safe for enterprise customers before turning on by default.
